consensus_summary: The blind consensus identifies the primary symbolic meaning of a garment as a person’s spiritual state or standing before God—especially righteousness and salvation. Clean/white/fine garments represent righteousness (imputed by God/Christ or the righteous deeds of the saints), salvation, and acceptance; filthy/soiled garments represent sin and guilt. Core texts repeatedly cited are Isa 61:10, Zech 3:3-5, Matt 22:11-12, Rev 19:8, Gal 3:27 and related white-robe passages. Alternatives (status/office, old/new self, body/resurrection, readiness, covering of shame) are recognized as common or minority but secondary. A noted intra-consensus debate exists specifically on whether Rev 19:8’s fine linen is imputed righteousness or the saints’ deeds.
book_summary: The book entry defines garment simply as “Righteousness — the righteous acts of the saints,” citing only Rev 19:8 (ASV/KJV fine linen = righteousness of saints) and cross-referencing a later chapter on garments & armor.
consensus_core_identification: spiritual standing/righteousness before God (imputed or deeds)
book_core_identification: righteousness as the righteous acts of the saints
boundary_disagreement: Book restricts the garment-of-righteousness sense exclusively to the saints’ own righteous acts, excluding or sidelining the equally common consensus reading of imputed/divine righteousness or covering for sin as itself the garment.
rationale: Minimum cores share the same central referent (righteousness). The book does not replace that referent; it merely selects and hardens one side of the well-attested Rev 19:8 debate already noted inside the consensus, thereby narrowing the extension of cases the symbol is allowed to cover. Differences are therefore boundary/precision refinements, not a contradictory core or novel identification. The single printed citation is the exact verse that licenses the book’s phrasing, so support is strong for the narrowed claim even while the claim itself is narrower than the consensus primary.
strongest_objection: Consensus primary meaning is broader (encompassing imputed righteousness, salvation, and divine covering) and treats the deeds-only reading of Rev 19:8 as one optional pole of an intra-consensus debate rather than the exclusive definition of the symbol.
